note: T30(b)'s bulk categorize pass, as data. Every rule below was written while looking at
the 977 real card rows T26b loaded — `npm run categorize:cards -- --report` prints the
same merchant-by-spend list these decisions were made from.
RULE OF INCLUSION: a rule exists here only where the issuer is WRONG, UNKNOWN, or
INCONSISTENT. Restating a category three issuers already agree on (every Chick-fil-A row
is already Food) would just be a second copy of their vocabulary, and it would bury the
rules that are doing work. So the set targets:
(i)   the 247 `Misc` rows — 27% of the ledger, the measurement that re-weighted T30;
(ii)  merchants two issuers categorize differently (UBER TRIP is Transportation on
Apple and Travel/Entertainment on Discover; GOOGLE is Utilities on some rows and
Other on others);
(iii) every Citi purchase, because Citi exports no category column at all and all 26
of its rows landed in `Misc` by default.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT RULED, so the gaps are a record rather than an oversight:
· HEALTHCARE (~$1,500: SMILES FOREVER, BACK IN THE GAME PT, ATLANTA REHABILITATION,
DERMATOLOGY AFFILIATES, NORTHSIDE HOSPITAL, PEACHTREE ORTHOPAEDIC, LABCORP, CVS,
WELLSTREET URG). The ledger vocabulary has no health category and inventing one is
not free: it needs a theme token (T38 shipped exactly three) and a CSP item to land
in, or it renders gray in `Other` and lands in Unassigned. This is the one real
vocabulary gap the data shows and it belongs to whoever adds the category.
· MIXED RETAIL (AMAZON*, TARGET, STAPLES, DOLLAR GENERAL, DEPOP, SP WINDSOR, PRINCESS
POLLY, ASOS, ABERCROMBIE). $1,227 of Amazon across 18 rows is groceries, tools,
clothes and gifts; `Misc` is the honest answer, not a failure to decide.
· PERSONAL CARE (barbershops, beauty supply, dry cleaning, spas).
· GENUINELY UNKNOWN merchants, which stay blank-by-default on purpose: SQ *MARY'S,
SIPPING PLANT LLC ($537), SPALANDGA, JESUS LOPEZ LLC, CITY OF ATLANTA (one issuer
calls it Gas/Automotive, the other Other — it could as easily be a water bill).
T30's acceptance criterion is that unknown merchants are left alone, never guessed.
A CAUTION ABOUT `contains` NEEDLES, learned from this corpus: there is no `APPLE` rule,
because Discover appends `APPLE PAY ENDING IN 2877` to every contactless row and Citi's
$4,000 balance transfer reads `BAL XFR. APPLE CARD-GOLDMAN SACHS BANK`. One three-letter
needle would have recategorized a transfer and a hundred unrelated charges. Needles are
chosen against the real strings, and `categorize:cards --report` shows the match count
of every rule before anything is written.

rules.name: Walmart
rules.why: 12 of Apple's 13 Walmart rows are already Grocery and the 13th is identical; Discover and Capital One both file the same store under Merchandise. Covers WALMART SUPERCENTER and WALMART STORE 03118.

rules.name: Wal Mart (spaced)
rules.why: Capital One writes the same store with a space — $508 across 6 rows that would otherwise miss the WALMART needle entirely.

rules.name: WM Supercenter
rules.why: The abbreviation Apple uses on returns. Without it the −$315.88 and −$273.90 refunds net against Misc instead of against the Groceries they came out of.

rules.name: Publix
rules.why: $1,054 across 18 rows. Already Grocery on Apple; the rule makes it independent of which card it lands on next.

rules.name: Kroger
rules.why: Grocery, every issuer, every row.

rules.name: Whole Foods
rules.why: The literal string on the statement is WHOLEFDS DCT 10687 — not `Whole Foods`, which is why the needle is spelled the way the issuer spells it.

rules.name: Sprouts
rules.why: Three different tails (MARKET / MARK / MARKET DECATUR) across three issuers: Discover says Supermarkets, Capital One says Merchandise, Citi says nothing. Needle stops before the tail.

rules.name: Aldi
rules.why: The one rule in this file that HAS to be a regex, and the dry run is what found it: `contains ALDI` matches EU KALDIS — Kaldi's Coffee — and quietly moved 44 Food rows into Groceries. A leading word boundary keeps ALDI INC and a future ALDI 54321 while excluding KALDIS. Capital One files the real Aldi rows as Merchandise.

rules.name: H Mart
rules.why: Korean grocery.

rules.name: Mariano's
rules.why: Chicago grocery; the apostrophe normalizes to a space.

rules.name: Dunkin'
rules.why: Citi's two rows ($24.92) are Misc for want of a category column. Store numbers are kept in the ledger's merchant string, so the needle has to be the stem.

rules.name: Cava
rules.why: Citi: 10148 CAVA DECATUR, three rows, uncategorized.

rules.name: Pisces
rules.why: Citi Square charge, restaurant. `SQ ` prefix kept so the needle can't collide with the word pisces elsewhere.

rules.name: Tandoori Pizza
rules.why: Citi, uncategorized; matches both the Square and the direct row.

rules.name: Rebel Teahouse
rules.why: Already Food on Apple's 8 rows; Citi's row was Misc. One rule makes the card irrelevant.

rules.name: Five Guys
rules.why: Citi writes 5GUYS 0539 ECOMM SANDY SPRINGS GA — digits are retained by normalization, so the needle starts with one.

rules.name: AMC Theatres
rules.why: Apple's 13 rows are Entertainment→Fun; Citi's two are Misc. Short needle, checked against the whole corpus: nothing else contains AMC.

rules.name: Steam
rules.why: Games, filed as Other by Apple.

rules.name: Bandcamp
rules.why: Music purchases, filed as Other.

rules.name: DramaWave
rules.why: A streaming app Discover files under Merchandise.

rules.name: Audible
rules.why: Audiobook subscription; Other on Apple, Other Services on Capital One.

rules.name: Amazon Prime
rules.why: The $15.89 monthly membership, not a purchase — and the longest-match tier is what keeps it out of the way of any future broad AMAZON rule. Fun rather than Bill because it is cancellable and mostly video; argue with it here rather than per row.

rules.name: Apple services
rules.why: iCloud/Apple One, $9.99 monthly. Needle deliberately not `APPLE` — see the caution in `note`.

rules.name: Apple (apple.com/bill)
rules.why: App Store / media billing, filed as Merchandise by Discover.

rules.name: LA Fitness
rules.why: Covers LA FITNESS, LA FITNS DECATUR CHU and LA FITNESS ANNUALFEE. A gym membership is discretionary; this keeps the annual fee with the monthly dues.

rules.name: Uber One
rules.why: A cancellable discount membership, not a ride: Apple filed it Transportation and Discover filed it Entertainment. Named longer than UBER TRIP so precedence is unambiguous either way.

rules.name: Viator
rules.why: $315 of tours and excursions that Apple files under Hotels→Misc. Delta's flights are already Transportation (Airlines), so this is the activity half of the same trip, not travel logistics.

rules.name: Spa (Jeju/Spa Land)
rules.why: GEORGIA SPA LAND SAU — a day spa, filed Other. Leisure, not healthcare: nothing here is prescribed.

rules.name: Spa Land (no spaces)
rules.why: $306 on one row where the same merchant arrives with the spaces already gone, so the SPA LAND needle misses it. Two spellings of one merchant is two rules — matching 'SPA' alone would be far worse.

rules.name: Uber (rides)
rules.why: The inconsistency that most needed a rule: 41 rows Transportation (Apple, Capital One) against 12 rows Fun (Discover calls it Travel/ Entertainment), same merchant, $843 total.

rules.name: Uber Eats
rules.why: Stated explicitly rather than left to the issuer, so that `UBER TRIP` and `UBER EATS` are two decisions on the record and nobody is ever tempted to write one broad UBER rule.

rules.name: Lyft
rules.why: Discover filed its two rows under Travel/ Entertainment→Fun. A ride is a ride.

rules.name: Tesla
rules.why: $506 across 20 rows averaging $25, plus TESLA SERVICE and TESLA SUPERCHARGER — charging and servicing a car, filed as Other by Apple and uncategorized by Capital One. Covers SUPERCHARGER through the stem.

rules.name: Supercharger
rules.why: Capital One drops the brand (SUPERCHARGER US), so the TESLA needle alone misses it.

rules.name: Parking
rules.why: One needle covers EMPIRE PARKING SERVICE, GLOBALAIRPORT PARKING, LAZ PARKING, PEAKPARKING COM and GSU PARKING DECK. Note it is PARKING and not PARK: `BAR TACO INMAN PARK` is dinner.

rules.name: University parking
rules.why: Campus deck; no PARKING in the string.

rules.name: AAA Park
rules.why: Hospital parking deck; needle is long enough not to catch the word park.

rules.name: SP+ Atlanta parking
rules.why: PSPT SPATL PRK — a parking operator that abbreviates past any readable needle.

rules.name: Quick Lane
rules.why: Tires and service, $271, filed Other.

rules.name: Pep Boys
rules.why: Auto parts and service, filed Other.

rules.name: Agero roadside
rules.why: Roadside assistance, filed Other.

rules.name: Car wash
rules.why: WHITECAP CAR WASH, filed Other.

rules.name: Traffic citation
rules.why: A court-payment processor; Apple itself calls one of the two rows Govt-services-parking and the other Other. Same merchant, so one answer.

rules.name: Express lane tolls
rules.why: USO LGBS I66 EXPRESS L — I-66 express lane tolls, $229, filed Other.

rules.name: American Home Shield
rules.why: Home warranty, $440 across 6 rows Apple already maps (Insurance→Bill) — but its −$125 credit row came through as Misc, so the refund was netting against the wrong category.

rules.name: Google
rules.why: 7 rows split 4 Bill (Apple: Utilities) / 3 Misc (Apple: Other) for storage and YouTube Premium. Following the issuer's own majority rather than my taxonomy; a subscription that is also a utility is a coin flip and consistency is the point.

rules.name: Hims & Hers
rules.why: $935 across 5 rows, ~$199 every month: a recurring prescription subscription. A standing monthly obligation reads wrong in a discretionary catch-all, and with no health category available Bill is the honest home.

rules.name: Termius
rules.why: Developer tooling subscription, $15/mo, filed Merchandise.

rules.name: GraphPad
rules.why: Software licence, $142, filed Services.

rules.name: OpenAI
rules.why: ChatGPT subscription, filed Merchandise.

rules.name: Intuit / TurboTax
rules.why: Covers INTUIT INC (already Bill) and INTUIT TURBOTAX (Misc) — tax filing, once a year, not discretionary.

rules.name: Georgia State tuition
rules.why: $2,398 — the single largest Misc line in the ledger. GA STATE UNIV PAYPATH and TN GA STATE UNIV PAYPA are tuition payments; Apple files both as Other. There is no education category, and Bill is where a fixed, non-negotiable obligation belongs. Deliberately does not match GSU PARKING DECK, which is parking.

rules.name: Apple Daily Cash
rules.why: An issuer reward, not a refund of anything. Left in Misc it nets against Misc spending, making a quarter of the ledger read lower than it was. `Adjustment` is already in the CSP's exclude set, which is the correct treatment of a card artifact (decision #21).

rules.name: Automatic statement credit
rules.why: Discover's recurring rewards credit — $31 across 8 rows, same reasoning as Daily Cash.

rules.name: Cashback bonus redemption
rules.why: Discover, $85 redeemed to the statement.

rules.name: Reward redemption
rules.why: Capital One's redemption row, which it labels Payment/Credit.

rules.name: Cash back reward
rules.why: Capital One, $34 across 2 rows.

rules.name: Mastercard transit offer
rules.why: A $2.50 promotional credit on both Rajna's cards; an offer, not a transport refund.
